text.p: Dutch firm Getronics NV said on Friday that it was looking for alternatives if its bid for state-owned payroll processor Roccade was unsuccessful. It also said it was eyeing takeovers in Spain, Scandinavia and Belgium.

"We are looking for (Dutch) alternatives in case we do not manage to acquire Roccade," Getronics chairman Ton Risseeuw told reporters, adding that the Dutch government had put too high a price on Roccade. He declined to elaborate.
Dutch media said last year that The Hague had delayed Roccade's privatisation because other parties, including U.S. Electronic Data Systems GME.N, had offered more money.
Risseeuw said the group first wanted to acquire Roccade before looking further afield. "We want to expand internationally, but a solid home base is necessary."
He said Roccade's sell-off was slated for July.
MeesPierson analyst Ajen Dibbets said Getronics was probably unwilling to accept a dilution of earnings per share with its bid for Roccade.
"This roughly means Getronics might not be willing to pay over 33 times Roccade's earnings," he said.
Roccade's first half 1996 operating profit was 10.1 million guilders.
Getronics generates some 30 percent of its turnover outside The Netherlands -- in Spain, Norway and Belgium -- but these activities contribute less than 30 percent of profits.
Risseeuw said Getronics position in Spain was too small, with just 200 staff in a nation of 50-60 million people.
Asked whether Getronics could buy Roccade and complete a major foreign acquisition, Risseeuw said the group could always issue new shares.
"That money would be forthcoming...we could always issue new shares," he said.
Getronics earlier announced 35 percent higher 1996 net profits of 131.6 million guilders.
